stimuli.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage
carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Popular culture often celebrates leaders who exude unshakeable confidence, mistakenly equating
(1)________ with competence. Charismatic figures who speak with unwavering certainty tend to captivate
audiences, while those who acknowledge doubt are sometimes dismissed as weak or indecisive. Yet a
growing body of research suggests that this perception may be fundamentally misguided.
Studies of organisational behaviour reveal that intellectually humble leaders, those willing to concede
the limits of their knowledge, frequently foster more innovative and resilient teams. By openly soliciting
dissenting views, such leaders create an environment in which employees feel emboldened to voice
unconventional ideas without fear of (2)________. In contrast, autocratic managers who brook no
disagreement often find themselves surrounded by sycophants, insulated from the unpalatable truths
essential for sound decision-making.
Humility, however, should not be conflated with (3)________. A humble leader is not one who vacillates
endlessly or abdicates responsibility; rather, it is one who weighs evidence judiciously before acting
decisively. The distinction is subtle but crucial, for excessive self-effacement can be as detrimental as
arrogance.
The most (4)________ leaders, it appears, strike a delicate balance between conviction and openness. They
possess the fortitude to make difficult choices while retaining the magnanimity to revise those choices
when confronted with compelling new information. Such adaptability is especially invaluable in an era
of rapid technological and economic flux.
Cultivating this balance is no trivial undertaking. It demands introspection, a (5)________ for honest
feedback and the courage to admit error publicly, qualities that, paradoxically, reveal genuine strength
rather than weakness.

explanations.cgl-2026-10-06:q:8:reviewed:df450f8572fe: Compare all the symbol strings character by character, including % versus $, 43 versus 48, and 23 versus 33. C,D,H match exactly.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-06:q:9:reviewed:47ec56d44cb8: Follow each arc and dot across the quadrants; the missing tile must preserve the orientation of the surrounding shapes. Rotation is explicitly disallowed.
